works.name: Fifty-Nine Salutes
works.subject: Shayrat airfield, Syria, 7 April 2017 local time.
label: Two miniature destroyers carry the visual authority of a fleet into the intimate space of a hat. Gold missile ornaments turn a strike into a ceremonial salute.
interpretation: The pairing of USS Ross and USS Porter gives the work a specificity that a generic warship would lack. Their reduction to elegant miniatures makes machinery of considerable destructive capacity available as personal distinction. The three rising ornaments organise that capacity into rhythm. Their resemblance to fireworks is an artistic transformation of the launch, giving a military action the manners of a celebration.
record: On 7 April 2017 in Syria, the United States launched 59 Tomahawk missiles from USS Ross and USS Porter at Shayrat airfield. It was still 6 April in Washington. The Pentagon described the strike as a response to the chemical attack three days earlier at Khan Shaykhun, identifying aircraft, shelters and supporting infrastructure as targets. This is the American account of the strike’s purpose and intended targets, not an independent assessment of its effects. 1 Khan Shaykhun and Shayrat were different sites. The OPCW Fact-Finding Mission subsequently confirmed exposure to sarin at Khan Shaykhun on 4 April. Its June 2017 report investigated chemical-weapons use, not the legality or strategic success of the American strike on Shayrat. 2
works.detail: Two gilded destroyers rise above an imagined airfield, while a separate pearl cluster introduces mourning. USS Ross and USS Porter were the documented launch vessels; the decorative missile arcs and miniature hangars are invented compositions. The pearls acknowledge the preceding chemical attack at Khan Shaykhun without representing a casualty count or placing that attack at Shayrat.

sources.label: Jim Garamone, U.S. Department of Defense, Trump Orders Missile Attack in Retaliation for Syrian Chemical Strikes, 6 April 2017 U.S. date. Official launch account.
OPCW, Report of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission in Syria Regarding an Alleged Incident in Khan Shaykhun, Syrian Arab Republic, April 2017, S/1510/2017, 29 June 2017. Chemical-use finding.

works.name: Mother of All Victories
works.subject: Achin district, Nangarhar, Afghanistan, 13 April 2017.
label: A large bomb becomes the jewel at the centre of a compact pillbox. The miniature refers to the GBU-43/B used against an ISIS-K tunnel complex in Afghanistan in April 2017.
interpretation: The bomb's popular nickname lends itself to a language of supremacy. In this work, the laurel wreath carries that implication further: the munition appears already rewarded. A measurement of explosive scale is made to resemble a judgment about success. The terrain resists this simplification. Its folds and openings suggest a place whose political and social complexity cannot be contained by the outline of a weapon.
record: On 13 April 2017, U.S. Forces Afghanistan announced that a GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast bomb had struck an ISIS-K tunnel complex in Achin, Nangarhar. The command described the strike as a way to reduce obstacles and danger for U.S. and Afghan forces conducting clearing operations. The named target was an ISIS affiliate within an ongoing conflict, not the Afghan population as a whole. 3 Afghanistan Analysts Network reported that restricted independent access initially made the effects difficult to verify beyond official statements. Its later account situated the strike within the continuing struggle for the Mamand Valley. The extraordinary size of the munition could be established; a durable strategic victory could not be inferred from size alone. The work’s dark fabric evokes aftermath but documents no particular civilian death. 4, 5
works.detail: The bomb rests inside a laurel halo above a small landscape of mountain folds and cave openings. The GBU-43/B and the Achin setting have historical counterparts, but their relative scale serves the artwork’s argument rather than engineering accuracy. The miniature caves are a composite invention. Black crystals and smoky organza suggest uncertainty and aftermath, not a verified damage survey or death toll.

sources.label: U.S. Forces Afghanistan, U.S. Forces Targets, Destroys ISIS-K Stronghold, 13 April 2017, release 2017-04-13-US-01. Official account.

Borhan Osman, Kate Clark and Martine van Bijlert, “Mother of All Bombs” Dropped on ISKP: Assessing the Aftermath, Afghanistan Analysts Network, 15 April 2017. Contemporary independent reporting and limitations of early evidence.
Borhan Osman, The Battle for Mamand: ISKP under Strain, but Not Yet Defeated, Afghanistan Analysts Network, 23 May 2017. Subsequent battlefield context.

works.name: The Allied Collection
works.subject: joint U.S., British and French strikes in Syria, 14 April 2018 local time.
label: Three jewel clusters turn a military coalition into an arrangement of coordinated luxury. Above them, a B-1 miniature and gilded missiles evoke the joint strikes on Syrian chemical-weapons-related facilities in April 2018.
interpretation: The word collection belongs naturally to fashion and quietly changes the meaning of coalition. Three states become coordinated elements of a designed whole. Their different constitutional practices and legal explanations disappear into harmonious colour. The hat's successful composition is therefore part of its argument: visual unity can stand in for an agreement that still requires scrutiny.
record: On 14 April 2018, American, British and French forces struck three facilities in Syria. The participating governments described them as connected to chemical-weapons research, storage or production; the U.S. account listed B-1 bombers among the platforms used. Officials said the operation was intended to degrade chemical capability and deter further use following the 7 April attack in Douma. The facilities’ alleged roles were part of the governments’ stated targeting case. 6 In 2023, an OPCW investigation found reasonable grounds to identify Syrian Arab Air Forces as responsible for the Douma attack. That later finding was not available when the allied strikes took place. The British government separately published a humanitarian-intervention justification, while House of Commons research documented the wider legal dispute. Allied participation and published legal arguments did not in themselves settle the operation’s legality. 7, 8, 9
works.detail: Three coordinated clusters of jewels stand for the American, British and French participants, making an alliance appear effortless and harmonious. The transparent vessels and miniature buildings evoke the stated chemical-weapons targets without reproducing a verified facility or recovered material. Douma, where the preceding chemical attack occurred, was separate from the sites struck a week later.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Defense, Pentagon Officials Describe Syria Strikes, Hope Assad Gets Message, 14 April 2018. Official operational account.
OPCW, OPCW Releases Third Report by Investigation and Identification Team, 27 January 2023; report S/2125/2023. Douma attribution.
UK Government, Syria Action — UK Government Legal Position, 14 April 2018. Participant's legal argument.
Richard Ware, The Legal Basis for Air Strikes against Syrian Government Targets, House of Commons Library, 16 April 2018, CBP-8287. Parliamentary research.

works.name: The Hunt
works.subject: raid on Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi's compound, northwestern Syria, 26–27 October 2019.
label: Helicopters circle a small compound as though the raid had become an orderly ceremonial dance. The setting refers to the operation that resulted in the death of ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi in October 2019.
interpretation: The circular arrangement promises enclosure. It gives the viewer a complete route around an event whose public account has required continuing examination. The miniature architecture makes the compound available as an object of visual mastery, while its recessed openings suggest spaces that remain difficult to see. The hat's neat perimeter becomes an imagined boundary around the story.
record: During the night of 26–27 October 2019, U.S. special forces raided the compound of ISIS leader Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi in northwestern Syria. U.S. officials said he detonated explosives as troops approached, killing himself and two children; they also described evacuating other noncombatants. Reuters subsequently reported ISIS’s confirmation of his death. The official description of the raid and the later confirmation of its principal outcome are distinct accounts. 10, 11 A 2023 NPR investigation, drawing on Pentagon records, questioned the military’s classification of people in a vehicle struck during the operation. This reporting raises a specific question about civilian harm without changing Baghdadi’s role as an ISIS leader or establishing that everyone at the compound was a combatant. The claims and the evidence behind them remain more complex than the neatly completed arc of the imagined headdress. 12
works.detail: Two model helicopters encircle a stylised compound, with a recessed passage visible beneath their ceremonial arc. Their route and the surrounding architecture are invented rather than a reconstruction of the raid. Dark pearls evoke mourning without counting fatalities. The separately reported dispute over a vehicle strike belongs to the historical account, not to any supposedly evidentiary object in the miniature.

sources.label: Jim Garamone, Central Command Chief Gives Details on Baghdadi Raid, U.S. Department of Defense, 30 October 2019. Official account of McKenzie's briefing.
Reuters, Islamic State Vows Revenge against U.S. for Baghdadi Killing, 31 October 2019. Confirmation and response.

Daniel Estrin, Pentagon Files Reveal Flaws in U.S. Claims about Syrian Casualties in Baghdadi Raid, NPR, 21 July 2023, updated 28 July; accessible NPR republication. Investigative reporting using released records.A-THRICE / THE MILLINERY–INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX • 56

works.name: Terminal Authority
works.subject: U.S. strike near Baghdad International Airport, Iraq, 3 January 2020 local time.
label: The drone lies close to the crown, its wings absorbed into the hat's elegant structure. Below it, a narrow road carries tiny vehicles through folds of black satin.
interpretation: This work makes distance look comfortable. The aircraft's long span becomes an architectural feature of a wearable object, while the road is partly concealed within the textile. The arrangement reproduces an imbalance of attention: the platform is available for admiration, while the place of impact requires a closer search. The immaculate surface makes control look like a property of the whole event.
record: On 3 January 2020, a U.S. strike near Baghdad International Airport killed Qasem Soleimani, commander of Iran’s Quds Force, Abu Mahdi al-Muhandis and others. The Pentagon described the presidentially directed action as protective and deterrent, asserting that Soleimani was planning attacks. Contemporary reporting described the aircraft as an MQ-9 Reaper, although the cited analysis noted that no official statement had publicly confirmed the platform. These accounts explain the declared purpose and reported weapon system without establishing a complete public record of the mission. 13, 15 In 2020, UN Special Rapporteur Agnès Callamard concluded that the strike violated international law and challenged the evidence supporting the U.S. self-defence rationale. Her assessment was an independent expert finding, not a criminal-court ruling. The fact that the president directed the operation addressed domestic command, but did not by itself determine whether its use of force met international-law requirements. 14
works.detail: The drone’s outstretched wing crosses an almost hidden road. Its recognisable shape follows published reporting on the aircraft, while the vehicles, road and fractured beads form a symbolic composite, not a map of the convoy or a damage record. No individual death corresponds to a bead. The composition places technical distance and political consequence inside one seemingly immaculate accessory.

sources.label: U.S. Department of Defense, Statement by the Department of Defense, 2 January 2020 Washington date. Official responsibility and rationale.
Agnès Callamard, Use of Armed Drones for Targeted Killings, 2020, A/HRC/44/38, including annex on the Soleimani strike. UN expert analysis.

Peter Lee, US-Iran Airstrikes: I Spent Two Years Learning about Reaper Drone Strikes, This Is How an Attack Plays Out, ABC / The Conversation, 8 January 2020. Reporting-based platform identification, with explicit uncertainty about official confirmation.

works.name: Over the Horizon
works.subject: U.S. counterterrorism air operations in Somalia, 2025; a composite reference.
label: A sweep of pearls draws a bright horizon between an aircraft ornament and a small mountain landscape. The veil makes the space between them difficult to see.
interpretation: The horizon promises a commanding view, but it also marks a limit. In this design, that limit is made desirable through pearls. The viewer is invited to appreciate the curve while the fabric below interrupts access to the terrain. Visibility becomes a privilege distributed by the image itself.
record: U.S. Africa Command stated that its 1 February 2025 strikes against ISIS-Somalia were coordinated with Somalia’s federal government. A separate July announcement concerned al-Shabaab west of Sabiid and did not disclose the assets used. These were different organisations and locations. Over the Horizon combines elements of a wider campaign rather than reconstructing one named operation or strike. 16, 17 Reuters reporting from areas recaptured by Puntland forces in February 2025 described a ground offensive and the experiences of residents alongside U.S. air operations. This local context matters: Somali authorities and communities appear here as participants with their own interests, not merely as the backdrop to distant aircraft. The aircraft in the image is deliberately generic, and its obscured terrain conveys no finding about casualties from a particular attack. 18
works.detail: A curve of pearls marks the horizon above a dark, cave-like recess. The mountainous forms chiefly evoke northern Somalia and operations against ISIS-Somalia; they do not relocate the separate al-Shabaab campaign to that terrain. No aircraft miniature identifies a verified platform for an individual strike. The veil transforms limited visibility into an aesthetic experience while leaving questions of actual harm to documented accounts.

sources.label: AFRICOM, Update: U.S. Forces Strike on ISIS-Somalia, 11 February 2025, concerning 1 February. Official account and coordination statement.
AFRICOM, U.S. Forces Conduct Strike Targeting al Shabaab, 26 July 2025, concerning 25 July. Separate location and asset-disclosure limits.
Reuters, Puntland Offensive Deals Blow to Islamic State in Somalia, 7 February 2025. Reporting from the ground.

works.name: Safe Passage
works.subject: Operation Rough Rider, Yemen, March–May 2025; the Ras Isa strike of 17 April provides a specific reference.
label: A carrier sits above a miniature port, surrounded by pearls and gold anchors. The upper composition celebrates the capacity to protect passage at sea; the lower one asks what happens to the workers and infrastructure through which ordinary commerce moves.
interpretation: The title sounds like a promise made to shipping. The image asks who is included in that promise. Aircraft and carrier form an orderly procession, while small loading structures and broken forms carry the less orderly experience beneath. The two settings occupy a single hat, resisting a clean division between the military operation and the commercial world it claims to secure.
record: Operation Rough Rider was the U.S. campaign against Houthi targets in Yemen from March to May 2025, conducted amid attacks on maritime shipping. On 17 April, CENTCOM acknowledged striking the Houthi-controlled Ras Isa fuel port and said the action sought to deny fuel and revenue to the group. Carrier aviation participated in the wider campaign, although the ornate carrier on this hat cannot be read as proof of the launch platform for each strike at Ras Isa. 19, 22 A June investigation by Human Rights Watch documented damage and civilian harm at the port, describing the attack as an apparent war crime requiring investigation. That was the organisation’s legal assessment, not a court verdict. On 6 May, Oman announced a U.S.–Sana’a ceasefire arrangement. The agreement was significant to this campaign but did not resolve the full range of regional hostilities. 20, 21
works.detail: A miniature carrier presides over bent loading structures, a crane and an empty safety helmet. Ras Isa was a fuel port, but the containers and industrial forms here are not a surveyed image of its layout. The helmet is an invented memorial to vulnerable workers, not a recovered possession. Black netting and fractured crystals visualise destruction without asserting a specific munition, impact point or casualty count.

sources.label: CENTCOM, Destruction of Houthi Controlled Ras Isa Fuel Port, 17 April 2025. Official acknowledgment and rationale.
Human Rights Watch, Yemen: US Strikes on Port an Apparent War Crime, 4 June 2025. Independent investigation and attributed legal assessment.
Foreign Ministry of Oman, Oman Announces Ceasefire Agreement between Washington and Sanaa, 6 May 2025. Mediator's announcement.
Heather Mongilio, Operation Rough Rider: 45 Days, 1,000 Targets, No End in Sight, USNI News, 29 April 2025. Contemporary campaign and carrier context.

works.name: Midnight Hammer
works.subject: U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities, 22 June 2025 local time.
label: The B-2's flying wing lends itself to the hat's controlled geometry. Gold edging makes its dark outline appear almost inevitable, while a miniature cross-section below opens a view into concealed space.
interpretation: Stealth becomes a visible luxury. The aircraft, designed to reduce detection, is displayed as the most desirable element of the image. Its strong silhouette supplies an impression of certainty. The pearls soften that geometry and help make force look compatible with impeccable taste.
record: Operation Midnight Hammer struck the Iranian sites at Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan on 22 June 2025 local time, the evening of 21 June in Washington. According to the U.S. military, B-2 bombers delivered ground-penetrating munitions at Fordow and Natanz, while submarine-launched cruise missiles were used at Isfahan. The single B-2 ornament condenses this multi-platform operation into one controlled silhouette. 23 On 23 June, the IAEA reported observable damage while cautioning that the full underground effects at Fordow had not yet been assessed. That was a dated technical assessment, not a permanent conclusion about the site. A presidential notification to Congress articulated an executive rationale, including collective self-defence of Israel; the existence of that notification did not itself determine the validity of the legal argument. 24, 25
works.detail: The bomber’s dark edge appears above a lavishly imagined underground cutaway. The B-2 was a documented platform, but the chambers below are not engineering drawings of Fordow, Natanz or Isfahan. Nothing in the miniature can establish the extent of destruction, the survival of particular facilities or the whereabouts of nuclear material. The image makes visual certainty seductive precisely where technical investigation remains necessary.

sources.label: Matthew Olay, U.S. Department of Defense / U.S. Strategic Command, Hegseth, Caine Laud Success of U.S. Strike on Iran Nuke Sites, 22 June 2025. Official operational account.
Rafael Mariano Grossi, IAEA Director General's Introductory Statement to the Board of Governors, 23 June 2025. Dated technical assessment and its limits.

Donald J. Trump, Letter to Congressional Leaders on United States Military Operations in Iran, 23 June 2025, preserved by the American Presidency Project. Executive notification and rationale.A-THRICE / THE MILLINERY–INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX • 57

works.name: Collateral Style
works.subject: U.S. strikes on alleged drug-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, 2025–2026.
label: A large naval ornament presides over much smaller boats. The contrast gives military power the scale of a public monument and life at sea the scale of a fragile detail.
interpretation: The title makes collateral harm sound like a desirable finish. Its discomfort depends on the ease with which a military term enters the vocabulary of fashion. The destroyer's polished surface offers the pleasure of an accomplished object. Nets, small hulls and an orange safety ornament complicate that pleasure through differences of scale and vulnerability.
record: U.S. forces began striking vessels alleged to be involved in drug trafficking in September 2025, and the campaign continued into 2026. An inspector-general report records the first attack on 2 September and attributes the cartel allegation to the military. Recording an attack is not the same as independently establishing the identity, cargo or legal status of everyone aboard. This artwork refers to the campaign as a whole, not a reconstructed individual incident. 26 The UN human rights chief and independent UN experts criticised the strikes under rules protecting the right to life and challenged the use of alleged criminal status as a sufficient basis for lethal force. These are attributed assessments, not claims proved by the digital image. The destroyer, nets, painted hulls and fragments are the artist’s symbols; they identify no particular firing platform or verified boat occupants. 27, 28
works.detail: A tiny hull and an empty orange life jacket sit beneath the outsized destroyer. The ship stands for naval power rather than a verified launch platform; the smaller boats and their colours are imagined. Neither the fishing-net lace nor the life jacket establishes that a particular targeted vessel was engaged in fishing or carried civilians. Their vulnerability is expressive, while identity and legality remain evidentiary questions.

sources.label: Lead Inspector General, Operation Southern Spear Report to Congress, January 1–March 31, 2026, published May 2026. Official oversight record, including attributed accounts of the campaign's beginning.
OHCHR, US Attacks in Caribbean and Pacific Violate International Human Rights Law: UN Human Rights Chief, 31 October 2025. Attributed assessment.

UN independent experts, United States: UN Experts Demand End to Unlawful Killings at Sea, as One-Year Death Toll Hits 223, 1 September 2026. Dated expert statement; the figure is not an independently adopted final total.

works.name: Hawkeye
works.subject: Operation Hawkeye Strike, Syria, beginning 19 December 2025.
label: A fighter and helicopter form a polished commemorative arrangement above a desert setting. Three pearl drops interrupt the gold decoration.
interpretation: The pearls are a limited memorial reference within a broader decorative vocabulary. Their number refers to three reported American deaths in the preceding attack; it is not a total for the subsequent operation. Keeping that distinction visible prevents commemoration from collapsing into a general justification for whatever follows.
record: CENTCOM named Operation Hawkeye Strike as the response to an attack near Palmyra on 13 December 2025 that killed two U.S. soldiers and one U.S. civilian interpreter. The subsequent strikes began on 19 December against sites described as ISIS infrastructure and weapons facilities. Reuters reported F-15 and A-10 aircraft, Apache helicopters and HIMARS among the systems used; CENTCOM also described support from Jordan. The headdress selects two aircraft from that wider operation. 29, 30 The three American deaths preceded Hawkeye Strike; they were not casualties of its retaliatory missions. Accordingly, the headdress’s three pearl drops commemorate those personnel, including the civilian interpreter, without suggesting a count of people killed during the later strikes or proof of the missions’ effectiveness. 31
works.detail: Three white pearls hang below the fighter and helicopter on a black ribbon. They commemorate the two U.S. soldiers and the U.S. civilian interpreter killed in the preceding 13 December attack, not deaths attributed to Hawkeye Strike. The desert setting is a composite rather than a mapped target site; the ribbon and pearls are invented memorial objects, not belongings recovered from the people commemorated.

sources.label: CENTCOM, CENTCOM Forces Remove ISIS Operatives in Syria after Large-Scale Strike, 30 December 2025. Official account connecting subsequent missions to Hawkeye's launch.
Reuters, US Hits ISIS in Syria with Large Retaliatory Strikes, Officials Say, 19 December 2025, subsequently updated. Platform and campaign reporting.
CENTCOM, U.S., Partner Forces Strike ISIS Targets in Syria, 10 January 2026. Explicit account of the two soldiers and U.S. civilian interpreter killed on 13 December.

works.name: The Christmas Strike
works.subject: U.S. strikes in Sokoto State, Nigeria, announced 25 December 2025.
label: A cruise missile rests among stars, pearls and seasonal ornament. The portrait draws on American strikes in Sokoto State, Nigeria, announced on Christmas Day 2025, placing the language of peace beside an instrument of force.
interpretation: Holiday imagery offers a ready-made atmosphere of generosity and peace. The missile is placed inside that atmosphere, where it receives the care given to a special gift. The arrangement makes military action appear compatible with seasonal benevolence while leaving the incompatibility available for inspection.
record: On 25 December 2025, AFRICOM announced strikes against targets it identified as ISIS-linked in Nigeria’s Sokoto State and said the operation was coordinated with Nigerian authorities. Reuters likewise reported Nigerian approval and cooperation. This context matters: the intervention cannot accurately be depicted as having proceeded in disregard of the Nigerian government’s stated participation. 32, 33 Published accounts differed over the weapons used. Reuters cited a U.S. official describing ship-launched Tomahawks, while a Nigerian statement later described MQ-9-delivered munitions. Subsequent reporting questioned elements of the operation’s effects and the identification of its targets. The gold missile therefore echoes one reported platform account rather than offering a definitive reconstruction; no particular launch vessel is identified. 33, 34, 35
works.detail: A gilded missile lies among seasonal stars above a dry, imagined landscape. Interwoven gold cords evoke reported American–Nigerian cooperation. The missile reflects one published account of the weapon system, alongside other differing accounts; neither the buildings nor the terrain reproduce a verified target site. Holiday ornament is the artist’s deliberate juxtaposition, while the dark veil is not evidence of civilian harm.

sources.label: AFRICOM, U.S. Africa Command Conducts Strike against ISIS in Nigeria, 25 December 2025. Official announcement and cooperation statement.
Reuters, Nigeria Averts Unilateral US Action by Cooperating on Airstrike, 26 December 2025. Cooperation and attributed Tomahawk account.
Reuters, U.S.-Backed Airstrikes in Nigeria Hit Two ISIS-Linked Camps, Government Says, 27 December 2025. Attributed Nigerian account, including different platform description.
The Washington Post, Unexploded Missiles, Witnesses Undercut Trump Account of Nigeria Strike, 10 January 2026. Investigative reporting on effects and identification limits.

works.name: The Extraction
works.subject: Operation Absolute Resolve, Caracas, Venezuela, 3 January 2026.
label: Helicopters rise above an imagined Caracas, tracing an ornamental golden route through its streets. The portrait refers to the U.S. operation that captured Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores in January 2026, questioning how a military action acquires the visual authority of a ceremonial procession.
interpretation: The route is the work's most bureaucratic ornament. It appears to connect a destination, an objective and a successful result without interruption. The city becomes an ordered passage through which authority travels. Gold supplies the appearance of legitimacy before the viewer has considered the legal questions raised by that journey.
record: On 3 January 2026, U.S. authorities announced that Operation Absolute Resolve had captured Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores in Caracas and transferred them to American custody for prosecution. Officials described a combined military and law-enforcement mission. The charges published in January and expanded in an October 2026 superseding indictment remain allegations, not findings of guilt. 36, 38 A December 2025 memorandum from the U.S. Office of Legal Counsel argued that the president had domestic constitutional authority for the operation. It was an executive legal opinion, not a ruling on its international-law implications. At the UN Security Council on 5 January, the secretary-general raised concerns about respect for international law. Together, these records show how operational success, domestic authorisation and international legitimacy remain distinct questions. 37, 39
works.detail: A gold processional route crosses fractured, miniature rooftops beneath the helicopters. The capture occurred, but these buildings, movements and breaks are imagined rather than a tactical map or photographic record of damage. The helicopters convey the operation’s military form without specifying an exact formation. The image questions whether successful capture can be confused with proof of criminal guilt or with legal authority for crossing a border.

sources.label: Matthew Olay, U.S. Department of War, Trump Announces U.S. Military’s Capture of Maduro, 3 January 2026. Official account of the operation.

U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Legal Counsel, Proposed War Department Operation to Support Law Enforcement Efforts in Venezuela, memorandum dated 23 December 2025, published January 2026. Executive-branch domestic-law analysis.

U.S. Attorney’s Office, Southern District of New York, Nicolás Maduro Moros and Cilia Adela Flores de Maduro Charged with Torture, 8 October 2026, announcing a further superseding indictment. Criminal allegations; not proof of guilt.
António Guterres, statement to the UN Security Council on Venezuela, delivered by Rosemary DiCarlo, 5 January 2026. UN institutional response.A-THRICE / THE MILLINERY–INDUSTRIAL COMPLEX • 58

works.name: Epic Fury
works.subject: U.S.–Israeli campaign against Iran beginning 28 February 2026; Operation Epic Fury is the U.S. designation.
label: The collection's richest arrangement gathers a miniature fleet into one ceremonial surface. Aircraft, ships and jewels compete for attention with a small group of empty schoolroom chairs.
interpretation: This work accumulates the collection's visual methods. The naval ornament returns, aircraft extend the image upwards and jewels bind distinct forms into a desirable whole. Escalation is expressed through the concentration of accomplishment in one object. The hat remains compact, making an extended campaign seem available to a single act of viewing.
record: CENTCOM announced the opening of Operation Epic Fury on 28 February 2026. The title belongs to the U.S. operation, while the portrait addresses the wider U.S.–Israeli campaign against Iran. Its ships, aircraft and damaged infrastructure form a deliberately compressed tableau; they are neither an exact order of battle nor an account of every action in the conflict. 40 In September 2026, a UN fact-finding mission found reasonable grounds to believe that U.S. strikes on the Shajareh Tayyebeh Primary School in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd amounted to war crimes. The mission characterised the first as an attack directed at a civilian object and the second as indiscriminate. These were investigative findings, not criminal-court judgments, and they did not attribute every civilian death in the wider campaign to the United States. 41, 42, 43
works.detail: A small cluster of empty schoolroom chairs appears beneath the fleet and pearls. The chairs are invented memorial forms, not photographed furniture from Minab, a casualty count or a reconstruction of the school. Their presence leads the eye from military display to the distinct incident examined by the September 2026 UN mission. The report’s findings stand on its investigation rather than on the emotional persuasiveness of these imagined objects.

sources.label: CENTCOM, U.S. Forces Launch Operation Epic Fury, 28 February 2026. Official opening announcement.

Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on Iran, Iran: Civilians Trapped between Extreme State Repression and Violations Arising from Devastating Conflict with US, Israel, UN Fact-Finding Mission Finds, 17 September 2026. Announcement of findings.

UN Human Rights Council, Report of the Independent International Fact-Finding Mission on the Islamic Republic of Iran, A/HRC/63/61, dated 14 September 2026, issued 21 September 2026. Investigative findings and evidentiary standard.
Reuters, UN Mission Finds Grounds to Believe US Committed War Crimes in Iran, and Tehran Crimes against Humanity, 17 September 2026. Independent coverage of the mission’s conclusions.

statement: The 1778 fashion print Coëffure à la Belle Poule offers an example of military commemoration becoming personal ornament. The French frigate appeared as a miniature ship above an elaborate coiffure, turning a celebrated but contested naval encounter into wearable prestige.

In thirteen AI-assisted digital couture portraits, A-Thrice translates contemporary American military equipment into exquisitely imagined millinery. Velvet, gold and pearls invite admiration before the viewer notices the small roads, harbours, boats, cave openings, and empty chairs below the machinery of power.

The operations are not interchangeable. Their purposes, legal justifications, and consequences differ. Beneath the Ornament therefore places documented events and attributed assessments beside artistic constructions, without treating a pearl, ruined building, or miniature as evidence of what happened to a particular person.

The imagined Victoria and Albert Museum provides the appearance of institutional legitimacy without claiming a real V&A exhibition, commission, or endorsement. The authority of a gallery label or a curated collection is itself under examination.

Victory Merch changes the scale of display. Haute couture becomes a red campaign cap: a portable declaration of belonging. Each emphatic triumphal slogan is immediately unsettled by its smaller, embroidered qualification.

The fictional gift shop makes the invitation to consume unmistakable. A souvenir, numbered edition, presentation box, or certificate can make an image of power seem rare, respectable, and worth owning. Yet a certificate can authenticate only the artwork, never the operation it depicts.

The completed digital catalogue is also a beautiful object that risks participating in the very culture of collection it critiques. That contradiction is intentional: the desire to possess is part of the work.
The objects are imaginary. The history is not.
